A_general.open_code_note: No official public server repository was found in the evidence bundle or official pages reviewed. The docs site exposes a separate documentation-search MCP server at https://docs.granola.ai/mcp; its tools are not tools of the meeting-notes endpoint.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: NOT FOUND; documentation specifies Streamable HTTP transport using the 2025-03-26 MCP transport specification, but does not state the server's negotiated protocol version.
A_general.release_status: Available on Granola plans; Enterprise access controls are documented. A February 2026 launch blog described Enterprise MCP as early-access beta.
other_official_servers: https://docs.granola.ai/mcp — separate documentation-search MCP server. Its manifest names search_granola_docs_help_center and documentation filesystem tools; excluded from this endpoint's actions.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP charge is listed. Access is available across plans, with capabilities and data range varying by plan. Basic is free; paid plans add history and some folder, search, and transcript access.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Basic: $0 per user/month; Business: $14 per user/month; Enterprise: $35 per user/month on the official pricing page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Per user per month. Basic access covers personal and public notes from the last 30 days. Business provides personal and public notes; Enterprise admins configure available scopes and MCP controls.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Browser OAuth or Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) for compatible clients. MCP operates for an individual Granola user and active workspace; no MCP API-key or service-account access. Enterprise admins control note scopes, transcript access, and whether changes are allowed. Published rate-limit guidance averages around 100 requests/minute across tools, subject to plan and change.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Granola controls plan capabilities and rate limits; Enterprise workspace admins configure scopes and feature switches; the user's identity and active workspace determine accessible notes.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official tool documentation lists nine tools without annotations. The official list is mostly reads; switch_workspace and sign_out change state. A third-party inventory names folder mutations and feedback. 2. Official docs do not describe server-enforced confirmation or elicitation. Third-party tool descriptions recommend explicit user intent for some folder operations; enforcement is unknown. 3. OAuth is per user; scopes and active workspace limit note access. Enterprise IdP can control who connects; workspace admins control note scopes, transcript access, and writes. 4. No URL-level tool filtering is documented. Enterprise can disable transcripts or set MCP read-only. Basic is limited to 30 days; workspace selection is active-workspace only. 5. Notes are limited to accessible personal/public scopes and active workspace. Third-party feedback description says reports exclude meeting content, names, IDs, and personal data and are screened. 6. Docs state rate limits vary by plan/tool and average around 100 requests/minute. Third-party inventory reports tool-specific concurrency limits, pagination, cursor expiry, and transcript chunks up to 80,000 characters; not corroborated by official docs. 7. Schemas and server-side validation are not published. Third-party descriptions give parameter-use rules; enforcement is unknown. 8. MCP-specific logs/audit trails are not documented. 9. Third-party `give_feedback` sends diagnostics to Granola; its description instructs agents to report unexpected behavior and says accepted reports are retained 90 days. 10. No server-delivered skill is documented; behavior rules appear in third-party tool descriptions. 11. Workspace and consent state affect future tool access; other memory behavior unknown. 12. The query tool is described by a third party as using an agent behind the tool; this does not establish a multi-server hierarchy. 13. No raw API, SQL, or script escape-hatch tool is listed.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list is https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/sharing/integrations/mcp and names 9 tools; no official total is stated. Agent Discoverability reports 14 tools and names six additional tools, but its displayed inventory omits the official switch_workspace name; the union therefore contains 15 names. Tedix reports 4 tools (get_meeting_transcript, get_meetings, list_meetings, query_granola), including query_granola rather than the official query_granola_meetings name. APIs.io reports 4 tools without names in the captured page. MartechDB says tool names are not known pending sign-in. The other current catalogue pages do not provide a more complete named list. Catalogue-only entries are marked third-party in actions.json. Tool schemas are not published in the official page or catalogue text.

actions.description: Ask natural-language questions across accessible meeting notes; returns cited answers.
List accessible folders and their metadata; paid plans only.
List accessible meeting notes, optionally filtered by folder on paid plans.
Read accessible meeting details, private notes, attendees, and summaries.
View screenshots or other attachments associated with a meeting.
Retrieve raw transcripts for accessible meetings; paid plans only.
Return connected account email, active workspace, and joined workspaces.
Change the active workspace in Granola and connected AI tools.
Revoke this MCP client's authorization for the connected Granola account.
Add a meeting note to a folder; may share it with folder viewers.
Create a top-level folder with private or workspace visibility.
Send sanitized diagnostics about unexpected tool behavior to Granola.
Remove a meeting note from a folder; may revoke others’ folder-derived access.
Search meeting metadata by keywords, participant, dates, or folder.
Rename a folder or change its description.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: MCP docs state there is no API-key or service-account access method for MCP; the separate Granola API is for scripts and custom integrations. Product note management and account deletion are documented, but corresponding MCP tools are not named in the official list. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official docs tell clients to use Streamable HTTP and OAuth metadata discovery, and recommend checking the connected account/workspace when notes are missing. The server-enforced status of client-facing recommendations is not established. Third-party tool descriptions contain explicit sequencing and consent guidance; enforcement is unknown.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Official docs state MCP returns notes available to the user in the active workspace and excludes notes from other workspaces; Enterprise admins can disable transcript access and make MCP read-only. Granola's security page says it does not store meeting audio and that notes are encrypted at rest and in transit. Privacy policy says third parties such as OpenAI or Anthropic are not allowed to train on personal data; Granola may train on de-identified data subject to settings, with Enterprise opted out by default.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Granola says MCP uses individual account authorization, follows workspace access settings, and allows admins to disable transcript and write access. Its security page describes user control over note sharing and deletion.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Workspace and Enterprise switches are documented controls. OAuth metadata confirms bearer-token authorization. The endpoint's exact note filtering, logging, transcript protection, retention, and confirmation implementation is not publicly inspectable. Third-party-described behavioral instructions are not verified as enforced server controls.

contradictions: The official MCP help page names nine tools, including switch_workspace. Agent Discoverability reports 14 tools but its captured list does not include switch_workspace and includes six additional names: add_note_to_folder, create_folder, give_feedback, remove_note_from_folder, search_meetings, and update_folder. The official FAQ describes folder note changes and feedback controls, but does not name these tools.
Tedix reports four names and uses query_granola; the official name is query_granola_meetings. Treat the Tedix name as an alternate catalogue label, not an additional native action.

Granola's current help page documents OAuth scopes and workspace restrictions. The OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises the resource scope mcp, while the authorization server's scopes_supported lists email, offline_access, openid, and profile. The docs' EMA configuration uses mcp as the resource scope; these are distinct metadata documents and their scope lists differ.
observations_for_research: The endpoint combines ordinary discovery/read tools with a natural-language query tool described by a third-party inventory as calling an internal agent.
Enterprise settings distinguish note categories, transcript availability, and write availability; the latter two switches apply workspace-wide.
switch_workspace is documented as changing the active workspace in the Granola app and other connected AI tools, so its effect extends beyond the current MCP client.
The feedback tool's third-party description includes data minimization, screening, and a stated 90-day retention period for accepted reports.
notes: Searched links.json, links_check.txt, all captured official pages and scripts, and the endpoint-origin pages.
